{{Current events|year=2019|month=01|day=25|content=

<!-- All news items below this line -->

;Disasters and accidents
*At least 59 people are killed when flooding and landslides hit [[Sulawesi]], [[Indonesia]]. Twenty-five others are missing and thousands have been displaced. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/01/rescuers-hunt-survivors-indonesia-floods-death-toll-rises-190125004129097.html (Al Jazeera)] [https://sg.news.yahoo.com/dozens-dead-thousands-displaced-flood-223924588.html?fbclid=IwAR1DduP4lWReGr1a9Cmq3IT3T40B2yBijvs7Dklp2wOAP-Ysruc1x8IBtXo (Yahoo! News)]
*A [[plane (aircraft)|plane]] and a [[helicopter]] collide over [[Testa del Rutor]] near the border of France and Italy, leaving five dead. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-47004710 (BBC)]
*A mining dam owned by the [[Brazil|Brazilian]] company [[Vale (mining company)|Vale]] collapses in [[Minas Gerais]], leaving a large number of people missing. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-47009118 (BBC)]

;Law and crime
*[[Special Counsel investigation (2017–present)]]
**[[Roger Stone]], a former adviser to [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]], is indicted by a federal grand jury and arrested on charges of obstruction, giving false statements, and witness tampering as part of special counsel [[Robert Mueller]]'s probe into [[Special Counsel investigation (2017-present)|Russian interference in the 2016 presidential election]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/donald-trump/ex-trump-adviser-roger-stone-arrested-part-mueller-probe-n962601 (NBC News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Macedonia naming dispute]]
** The [[parliament of Greece]] votes 153–146 in approval of changing the name of the [[Republic of Macedonia]] to the Republic of North Macedonia, ending a 27-year [[Macedonia naming dispute|naming dispute]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-47002865 (BBC)]
*[[2018–19 United States federal government shutdown]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] announces a short-term deal has been reached with congressional leaders to temporarily reopen the federal government after a [[2018-19 United States federal government shutdown |partial shutdown]] that has lasted for 35 days. The stop-gap agreement will last three weeks, until February 15, and will allow for talks to continue over security on the [[Mexico-United States border]]. The temporary deal includes no money for President Trump's [[Immigration policy of Donald Trump|planned border barrier with Mexico]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/donald-trump/trump-shutdown-announcement-n962836?fbclid=IwAR1Rk9IGd8iTTzf-Pa29x0qRLf5ONIJlUEdCEZEKDAl3zp9qWseeXkxGjgc (NBC News)]
*[[2020 United States presidential election]], [[2020 Democratic Party presidential primaries]]
**Retired U.S. Army Major and former West Virginia State Senator [[Richard Ojeda]] suspends his campaign for presidency in 2020 presidential election. [https://theintercept.com/2019/01/25/richard-ojeda-president-drops-out/ (The Intercept)]

;Science and technology
*[[Facebook]] will merge the messaging services of [[WhatsApp]], [[Instagram]] and [[Facebook Messenger]] by early next year, according to reports. The move will allow users to cross-message others on all three apps, though they will continue to function independently. [https://www.independent.co.uk/life-style/gadgets-and-tech/news/facebook-instagram-whatsapp-messenger-app-merger-download-a8746376.html (The Independent)] [https://www.theweek.co.uk/99227/facebook-to-merge-messenger-with-instagram-and-whatsapp-in-early-2020 (The Week)]
